judged_text: The spec rewrite deletes every edge-case membership test (normal-group rename via update, 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users', non-member removal, incremental add/delete) and replaces them only with happy-path specs plus the automatic-group guards, so the new endpoints' edge behaviors are unguarded. A future change to Admin::GroupsController#update's flat-param handling or to add_members' find_by_username loop — e.g., breaking rename for normal groups, whose only spec was deleted here — passes CI and ships silently, since nothing pins update's positive-path behavior or the new endpoints' handling of unknown users/non-members.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes several prior edge-case specs around membership and updates (the whole prior “incremental” PATCH add/delete block, non-existent user add, non-member removal, and normal-group rename/member update via `update`). In the new spec file, coverage is mostly happy-path for `add_members`/`remove_member` plus automatic-group 422 guards, and `update` is only tested for automatic-group name-ignore. Meanwhile, the controller logic has materially changed: `Admin::GroupsController#update` now reads flat params (`params[:name]`, `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`) and membership changes moved to `add_members` (looping `User.find_by_username`) and `remove_member` (`group.users.delete(user_id)`). Those new/changed behaviors (e.g., normal-group rename in `update`, handling unknown usernames in `add_members`, removing a non-member) are no longer pinned by tests, making future regressions more likely to slip through CI. This is a concrete test-coverage regression, not a direct functional defect shown by the diff itself.
